title: NVLink-aware batch packing and kernel orchestration for multi-GPU attention
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Summary:
We need to reduce cross-GPU transfer overheads and improve kernel throughput for long-context attention workloads running on multi-GPU nodes (H100 / L40S / A10). Current prefill+decode scheduling frequently interleaves requests across GPUs in a topology-agnostic manner, causing NVLink saturation and suboptimal kernel shape choices. This ticket implements NVLink-aware batch packing, topology-informed kernel selection, and a prefill placement heuristic to keep attention KV/prefixes local when possible.

Background:
- Observed p99 decode latency regressions for distributed workloads when sequence lengths exceed 8k — bottlenecked on NVLink interconnects rather than raw kernel compute.
- Kernel selection logic currently picks kernels based on single-GPU heuristics (sequence length, dtype) without considering inter-GPU transfer cost or contiguous KV locality.
- Mixed MIG/A10 partitioned nodes expose asymmetric bandwidth/latency; naive round-robin scheduling moves tokens between partitions causing stalls.

Goals:
1) Implement batch packing that preferentially groups requests by on-node NVLink locality and by model sharding assignment (when TP/DP are in use).
2) Extend kernel selector to account for cross-card transfer cost penalty; prefer kernels that increase compute per-transfer (bigger tile sizes, fused attention) when NVLink cost dominates.
3) Add a prefill placement heuristic: for long-context sessions, attempt to co-locate prefill and subsequent decode on the same GPU or same NVLink fabric to avoid repeated KV migration.

Constraints / Success criteria:
- No functional changes to model outputs (numerical parity within acceptable FP/quantization tolerances).
- Improve p99 decode latency by >=15% on H100 8x (NVLink) cluster for 8k–32k seq workloads in our internal benchmark.
- Maintain or improve throughput (tokens/sec) for short-context workloads (<2k) within 5% of baseline.

Acceptance Criteria (high level):
- NVLink-aware packing is enabled behind a runtime flag and has unit/integration tests.
- Kernel selector exposes a cost model parameter (transfer_cost_weight) and default tuned values for H100/L40S/A10.
- Validation dashboards show p50/p95/p99 improvement and no regressions in accuracy tests.

Approach (technical):
1) Topology discovery: extend node agent to expose a compact topology map (GPUs, NVLink groups, bandwidth estimates, MIG partitions for A10). Use existing NVML + NCCL topology queries.
2) Packing policy: during request routing phase, compute locality score for each request relative to in-flight batches and available GPUs; pack batches to maximize intra-NVLink locality. Implement greedy first-fit heuristic with fallback to bandwidth-proportional distribution.
3) Kernel cost model: augment kernel selector to incorporate an estimated transfer_cost = bytes_sent / effective_bandwidth_topology. Final kernel score = alpha * compute_time + beta * transfer_cost. Expose alpha/beta knobs and default per-hardware profiles.
4) Prefill placement heuristic: for sessions with > prefill_threshold_tokens, pin prefill to a GPU and try to direct subsequent decode requests to the same GPU for the session lifetime (or until memory pressure forces migration). Integrate with our existing routing policy and session affinity table.
5) MIG/A10 handling: treat each MIG slice as an isolated node when computing locality; prefer intra-slice scheduling. For asymmetric partitions, adjust effective_bandwidth_topology accordingly.
6) Async transfers: where cross-GPU transfers are unavoidable, overlap NVLink DMA with host scheduling and prefetch KV shards ahead of decode using an extra DMA worker pool.

Experiments (planned):
- Perf harness: run standard long-context attention benchmark on 8x H100 NVLink nodes, 4x L40S (NVLink topology differs), and A10 partitioned nodes (various MIG shapes).
- Ablations: (a) packing-only, (b) kernel cost-only, (c) prefill-affinity-only, (d) all combined.
- Sensitivity sweep across alpha/beta to find robust defaults.

Metrics / Success metrics (measurable):
- p99 decode latency reduction >=15% for 8k–32k seq on H100 (primary).
- tokens/sec change within +/-5% for short seq (<2k).
- NVLink utilization reduced (measured as sustained inter-GPU GB/s) for long-context mixes.
- Memory fragmentation and OOM events not increased by >1 per 100k requests compared to baseline.

Risks & Trade-offs:
- Adding topology-aware heuristics increases scheduler complexity and edge-case behavior under rare topologies.
- Aggressive prefill pinning can increase memory pressure on single GPUs, leading to fragmentation or evictions. Mitigation: add memory-watermark sensors and fallback policy.
- Kernel changes may interact with quantization/graph fusion and require re-validation of numeric quality.

Dependencies:
["ENG-35892", "ENG-41107"]

Links (artifacts / dashboards / PRs):
- Design doc (internal): https://docs.internal.redwood.ai/runtime/nvlink-packing-design
- Perf dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.internal.redwood.ai/d/attn-nvlink/long-context
- Draft PR (kernel selector): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428
- Draft PR (scheduler): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1431

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1: topology discovery + unit tests (complete)
- Week 2: packing policy + integration tests (in progress)
- Week 3: kernel cost model and alpha/beta sweep (blocked by PR review)
- Week 4: prefill placement + perf runs and dashboard updates
- Week 5: stability run, docs, and release gating (runtime-1.20)

Progress updates:
- 2025-02-12 (Asha Rao): Created ticket and initial design sketch. Identified problematic workloads from telemetry (long-context chatbot workload #C-304).
- 2025-02-14 (Miguel Torres): Implemented topology exporter prototype; unit tests added. Patch: PR 1428 (WIP).
- 2025-02-17 (Emma Li): Integration test for greedy packing shows initial p99 improvement of ~9% on H100 8x for 8k seq (packing-only). Noted increased memory concentration on GPU-2 in our cluster; added memory-watermark fallback change request.
- 2025-02-20 (Miguel Torres): Kernel selector changes landed behind feature flag; alpha/beta default set for H100 in config; beginning ablation runs. Observed NVLink TX bytes drop by ~12% in packing+selector combined run.

Reviewers & stakeholders:
["Ravi Patel (runtime)", "Sofia Nguyen (perf)", "Emma Li (infra)"]

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default alpha/beta tradeoff for L40S (recommended: bias more toward compute due to lower NVLink saturation recorded in L40S clusters).
- Prefill pinning TTL: how long should we keep a session pinned before allowing migration? Proposed default 5 minutes.

Next steps:
- Finish alpha/beta sweep and run full perf suite across H100/L40S/A10 MIG shapes.
- Address memory concentration fallback and complete integration tests.
- Prepare release notes and enable behind runtime-1.20 gradual rollout flag for select customers.
